statement: Keep a written risk process for each high-risk AI system and update it as the system changes.
Check that data used to build and test the system is relevant, representative and free of known errors.
Prepare documents that describe the system's design, purpose and limits before it goes live.
Let the system log events automatically so its operation can be traced afterwards.
Tell people when they are dealing with an AI system and give instructions for use.
Design the system so a trained person can oversee it, intervene and stop it.
State the expected accuracy and keep the system resistant to errors and attempts to manipulate it.
Register each high-risk system in the public database and keep the entry current.
Have someone other than its builders assess the system before first use and again after a substantial change.
Collect and review data on the system's performance after it is in use and act on what it shows.
Run a quality management system with written policies, named roles and set procedures.
Obtain the provider's instructions and documentation and hold the provider to them when you deploy its system.
Keep a complete list of models in use, with purpose, owner and status.
Have staff independent of development validate a model before use and on a regular cycle.
Track model performance in use against set thresholds and escalate breaches.
Have senior management approve a model risk policy that assigns roles and limits.
Document model design, assumptions and limits so an outside reader can follow them.
Apply the same validation and monitoring to vendor models as to models built in-house.
Identify and measure model risk and keep it inside a stated appetite.
Assess the quality and fit of the data that feeds a model.
Compare model outputs with actual outcomes and investigate gaps.
Make sure users of model output can challenge it and override it where warranted.
Keep a record of each model's decisions and changes so they can be reviewed later.
Review changes to models and their uses before they go into production.
Set policies, roles and accountability for managing AI risk across the organization.
Maintain an inventory of AI systems, including those supplied by third parties.
Manage risks that come from third-party AI components and data.
Record each system's context, intended purpose and the people it may affect.
Select metrics and test the system for the risks identified.
Prepare a plan for AI incidents, name who responds and tell affected parties when one happens.
Define the roles people play in overseeing AI output and when they step in.
Explain system outputs and limits to the people who use or are affected by them.
Evaluate whether the system is valid, reliable, secure and able to recover from failure.
Monitor deployed AI systems for changes in behavior and for new risks.
Involve assessors who did not build the system when evaluating it.
Understand the origin, quality and suitability of the data the system uses.
Tell a declined applicant the specific principal reasons for the decision.
Make sure the reasons given are the factors the scoring model actually used.
Notify the applicant of the decision within the period the bank has set.
Send a notice for incomplete or countered applications on the same clock.
Keep application and decision records for the period the bank has set.
Give applicants the standard notice of their rights with each adverse decision.
Keep prohibited-basis information out of model inputs and test for proxies.
Maintain a fair lending compliance program with named owners.
Watch decision outcomes and reason patterns for unexplained differences between groups.
Check that a purchased scoring model can produce accurate reasons.
Document how the model's reason codes are derived from its inputs.
Have the reason-code logic tested by someone who did not build it.
